symbols.name: V
symbols.def: \(V\) indexes the observed variables.

symbols.name: Xv
symbols.def: \(X_v\in\{0,1\}\) is the observed variable at vertex \(v\in V\).

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: \(G=(V,E^{\to},E^{\leftrightarrow})\) is the latent projection of a recursive semi-Markovian causal model.

symbols.name: Edir
symbols.def: \(E^{\to}=\{(w,v):w\to v\text{ in }G\}\).

symbols.name: Ebi
symbols.def: \(E^{\leftrightarrow}=\{\{v,w\}:v\leftrightarrow w\text{ in }G\}\).

symbols.name: pa
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{pa}_G(v)=\{w\in V:(w,v)\in E^{\to}\}\).

symbols.name: districts
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D(G)\) is the partition of \(V\) into maximal bidirected-connected sets.

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: \(M\) assigns at most one sign to each directed edge whose parent effect is restricted.

symbols.name: Sv
symbols.def: \(S_v=\{w\in\operatorname{pa}_G(v):((w,v),s)\in M\text{ for some }s\in\{+1,-1\}\}\).

symbols.name: rv
symbols.def: \(r_v=|\operatorname{pa}_G(v)\setminus S_v|\).

symbols.name: Dm
symbols.def: \(D_m\) is the number of up-sets of the Boolean lattice \(\{0,1\}^m\), equivalently the number of isotone Boolean functions on \(m\) coordinates.

symbols.name: UG
symbols.def: \(U_G=\{u_v:v\in V\}\cup\{u_e:e\in E^{\leftrightarrow}\}\), with one private latent index per vertex and one shared latent index per bidirected edge.

symbols.name: chU
symbols.type: observed children of an exogenous index
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{ch}(u_v)=\{v\}\) and \(\operatorname{ch}(u_{\{v,w\}})=\{v,w\}\).

symbols.name: CU
symbols.def: \(C(u)\) is the maximal set of observed vertices reachable from \(\operatorname{ch}(u)\) through a chain of exogenous indices with successive indices sharing an observed child; in the latent projection it is the district containing \(\operatorname{ch}(u)\).

symbols.name: bU
symbols.def: \(b_u=\prod_{v\in C(u)}T_v\).

symbols.name: RGM
symbols.def: \(R_{G,M}=\prod_{u\in U_G}b_u\).

symbols.name: fv
symbols.def: \(f_v\) is the recursive response mechanism for \(X_v\).

symbols.name: OmegaU
symbols.def: \(\Omega_u\) is the support of the canonical exogenous variable indexed by \(u\in U_G\).

symbols.name: muU
symbols.def: \(\mu=\bigotimes_{u\in U_G}\mu_u\) is the product law of the semi-Markovian exogenous variables.

symbols.name: mfrak
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak m=(f,\mu)\) consists of binary structural mechanisms \(f_v\) and mutually independent exogenous laws indexed by \(U_G\).

symbols.name: Mclass
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak M(G,M)\) is the class in Definition \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: \(K\) is fixed and finite.

symbols.name: AQ
symbols.space: finite conjunctions of binary potential-response literals
symbols.def: \(A_Q\) is a finite unnested event over potential responses generated by \(G\).

symbols.name: BQ
symbols.space: finite conjunctions of binary potential-response literals
symbols.def: \(B_Q\) is a finite unnested event over potential responses generated by \(G\).

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: \(Q=(A_Q,B_Q)\) denotes the query \(P(A_Q\mid B_Q)\).

symbols.name: thetaQ
symbols.def: For every \(\mathfrak m\) with \(P_{\mathfrak m}(B_Q)>0\), \(\theta_Q(\mathfrak m)=P_{\mathfrak m}(A_Q\cap B_Q)/P_{\mathfrak m}(B_Q)\).

symbols.name: kappa
symbols.def: \(\kappa\) is a fixed positive constant.

symbols.name: OQ
symbols.def: \(\mathsf O_{G,M}(Q)\) is the construction in Definition \(\mathrm{def:order\text{-}amwn}\).

symbols.name: NQ
symbols.space: finite signed sums of district order cells
symbols.def: \(\mathsf N_{G,M}(Q)\) is the construction in Definition \(\mathrm{def:order\text{-}normal\text{-}form}\).

symbols.name: FAIL
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{FAIL}\) records that no identifying expression was returned by the procedure.

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: \(\alpha\) indexes a two-sided Wald confidence interval.

symbols.name: Acan
symbols.def: \(A_{G,M}=\prod_{v\in V}T_v^{\prod_{u\in U_G:\,v\in\operatorname{ch}(u)}b_u}\).

symbols.name: Wk
symbols.def: \(W_k\subseteq V\) is the vertex set intervened upon in regime \(k\); \(W_k=\varnothing\) denotes the observational regime.

symbols.name: wk
symbols.def: \(w_k\in\{0,1\}^{W_k}\) is the constant assignment imposed on \(X_{W_k}\) in regime \(k\).

symbols.name: Zmenu
symbols.def: \(\mathcal Z=\{z_1,\ldots,z_K\}\) with \(z_k=\operatorname{do}(X_{W_k}=w_k)\), where \(W_k\subseteq V\), \(w_k\in\{0,1\}^{W_k}\), and \(W_k=\varnothing\) denotes observation. No stochastic intervention kernel is implicit.

symbols.name: PZ
symbols.def: \(P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m)=(P_{\mathfrak m,z_k}(X_V=x):1\le k\le K,\ x\in\{0,1\}^{V})\).

symbols.name: Fiber
symbols.def: \(\mathcal F_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(p)=\{\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M):P_{\mathfrak m,z_k}(X_V)=p_k\text{ for every }k\}\).

symbols.name: IDcrit
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{GID}_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(Q)\) is the global menu-equivalence criterion in Definition \(\mathrm{def:identification\text{-}criterion}\).

symbols.name: Rexpr
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R(p)\) is the grammar in Definition \(\mathrm{def:expression\text{-}grammar}\).

symbols.name: CTFID
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{CTFID}\) is the procedure of Correa, Lee, and Bareinboim.

symbols.name: MID
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{MID}\) is Algorithm 1 of Maiti, Plecko, and Bareinboim.

symbols.name: pstar
symbols.def: \(p^{\star}=P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_0)=P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_1)\) for a compiled nonidentification pair.

symbols.name: trace
symbols.def: \(\tau_{\mathsf F}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)\) records the two canonical structural profiles, exact algebraic product-simplex masses, sign conditions, positive denominators, common menu vector, and unequal query cross-product returned by the satisfiable nonidentification system.

symbols.name: nk
symbols.def: \(n_k\) is the independent sample size from regime \(z_k\).

symbols.name: rhok
symbols.def: \(\rho_k=\lim_{n\to\infty}n_k/n\).

symbols.name: phat
symbols.def: \(\widehat p=(\widehat p_1,\ldots,\widehat p_K)\), where \(\widehat p_k\) is the empirical multinomial cell vector in regime \(k\).

symbols.name: F
symbols.def: \(F\) is the finite expression returned by \(\mathsf{MCTFID}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)\).

symbols.name: lambdaF
symbols.def: \(\lambda_F(p)\) is the minimum absolute value, at \(p\), of every branch guard, every active-branch division denominator, every active isolated-root derivative, and every active root-to-isolating-interval endpoint distance in the finite expression tree \(F\); the minimum of an empty list is \(1\).

symbols.name: thetaHat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\theta_Q=F(\widehat p)\).

symbols.name: Sigmak
symbols.def: \(\Sigma_k=\operatorname{diag}(p_k)-p_kp_k^{\mathsf T}\).

symbols.name: sigma2
symbols.def: \(\sigma_F^2(p)=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\rho_k^{-1}\nabla_kF(p)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_k\nabla_kF(p)\).

symbols.name: sigmaHat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\sigma_F\) is obtained from \(\sigma_F(p)\) by substituting \(\widehat p_k\), \(n_k/n\), and the recursively evaluated gradients.

symbols.name: CI
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{CI}_{1-\alpha}\) is the interval in Definition \(\mathrm{def:wald\text{-}interval}\).

symbols.name: Mpub
symbols.type: published common-input binary CGMA/general-SCM model class
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{PB}}^{\mathrm{bin}}(G,M)\) is the broader model class in Definition \(\mathrm{def:published\text{-}binary\text{-}cgma\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: MIDplus
symbols.type: signed order-closure extension of the published monotonicity-aware procedure
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{MID}^{+}\) is the finite order-closure precheck and fallback procedure in Definition \(\mathrm{def:midplus\text{-}order\text{-}closure}\).

assumptions.condition: \(V\) is finite and \(X_v\in\{0,1\}\) for every \(v\in V\).
\(G\) is acyclic and \(\mathfrak m\) has the recursive semi-Markovian expansion indexed by \(U_G\).

For every \(((w,v),s)\in M\), every latent assignment, and every fixed assignment of \(\operatorname{pa}_G(v)\setminus\{w\}\), the map \(x_w\mapsto f_v(x_{\operatorname{pa}_G(v)},u)\) is nondecreasing when \(s=+1\) and nonincreasing when \(s=-1\).
There exists one \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\) such that \(P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m)=p\).

standard.name: positive denominator for conditional counterfactual reduction

assumptions.condition: Within regime \(k\), the \(n_k\) observations are independent draws from \(p_k\), and samples from distinct regimes are independent.

standard.name: regular point of a finite piecewise-analytic functional, including a locally fixed branch

definitions.name: signed response types
definitions.construction: For each \(v\), sign-normalize a restricted parent by \(z_w=x_w\) for sign \(+1\) and \(z_w=1-x_w\) for sign \(-1\); a local type is a map assigning to every unrestricted-parent configuration an up-set of \(\{0,1\}^{m_v}\), so its count is \(T_v=D_{m_v}^{2^{r_v}}\).

definitions.name: canonical response bound
definitions.construction: Assign each \(u\in U_G\) at most \(b_u=\prod_{v\in C(u)}T_v\) support points; the induced joint latent assignment space has at most \(R_{G,M}=\prod_{u\in U_G}b_u\) points, and the vector of free exogenous masses has dimension at most \(\sum_{u\in U_G}(b_u-1)\).

definitions.name: Fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(p)=\{\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M):P_{\mathfrak m,\operatorname{do}(X_{W_k}=w_k)}(X_V=x)=p_k(x)\text{ for every }x\in\{0,1\}^{V}\text{ and }1\le k\le K\}\) for the specified deterministic hard-intervention menu \(\mathcal Z=\{\operatorname{do}(X_{W_k}=w_k):1\le k\le K\}\), with \(W_k=\varnothing\) representing observation.

definitions.name: global signed-monotone functional-identification criterion
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{GID}_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(Q)=1\) exactly when, for every \(\mathfrak m_0,\mathfrak m_1\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\) with \(P_{\mathfrak m_i}(B_Q)>0\), \(P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_0)=P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_1)\) implies \(\theta_Q(\mathfrak m_0)=\theta_Q(\mathfrak m_1)\).

definitions.name: OQ
definitions.construction: Construct the ordinary ancestral multi-world network for the literals in \(A_Q\cup B_Q\); merge copies licensed by consistency and exclusion; sign-normalize every parent coordinate in \(S_v\); and annotate each pair of copies of \(X_v\) by the induced Boolean-lattice order relation between their normalized parent assignments. The resulting finite labeled mixed graph is \(\mathsf O_{G,M}(Q)\).

definitions.name: NQ
definitions.construction:
Apply the following construction separately to \(E=A_Q\cap B_Q\) and \(E=B_Q\). Let \(\mathcal T_v\) be the finite set of signed-isotone complete local response tables specified by Definition \(\mathrm{def:signed\text{-}response\text{-}types}\), and let \(R_v\) denote the realized complete local response table. For every \(t=(t_v)_{v\in V}\in\prod_{v\in V}\mathcal T_v\), recursively evaluate the literals of \(E\) in topological order in \(\mathsf O_{G,M}(Q)\), after deleting every local restriction inconsistent with the normalized Boolean-lattice order. If \(e_E(t)\in\{0,1\}\) is the resulting event indicator, define
\[
 \mathsf N_{G,M}(Q;E)
 =\sum_{t:e_E(t)=1}\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}
 \mathbf 1\{(R_v)_{v\in D}=t_D\},
\]
with terms ordered lexicographically by a fixed ordering of vertices and local tables. The two forms for \(A_Q\cap B_Q\) and \(B_Q\) constitute \(\mathsf N_{G,M}(Q)\). Thus the normal form is the expansion in the fixed exact response-type atom basis, rather than an unspecified choice among algebraically equivalent M\"obius expansions.

definitions.name: Rexpr
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal R(p)\) is the grammar of finite expression trees containing menu cells and rational constants and closed under finite sums, products, quotients on guarded positive denominators, and finite total branches guarded by rational polynomial sign conditions.  Its algebraic-section terms are \(\operatorname{Root}_j(h;I)\), when the active branch certifies that the rational interval \(I\) contains exactly the indexed real root of \(h(t,p)\), and \(\operatorname{ThomRoot}_{\sigma}(h)\), the unique real root whose derivative-sign vector has the finite Thom encoding \(\sigma\) on the active semialgebraic branch.  Every root term carries an existence-and-uniqueness guard, and every expression has a rational default on branches where that guard fails.  The polynomial \(h\) and all branch guards have rational coefficients.  At an arbitrary population vector \(p\), exact symbolic evaluation means evaluation in the ordered real field supplied with exact polynomial-sign queries: the active guard is selected by its exact sign vector and each root term denotes its uniquely certified real section.  When the coordinates of \(p\) are given exactly as rational or real-algebraic numbers, this semantics is implemented by a finite standard algorithm using algebraic arithmetic, sign determination, Thom encodings, and real-root isolation.  No finite bit-computation claim is made for an arbitrary transcendental input encoding without such a sign oracle.

definitions.name: MCTFID
definitions.construction:
Define the exact finite response-profile oracle \(\mathsf{MCTFID}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)\) for a menu \(\mathcal Z=\{z_k:1\le k\le K\}\) of specified deterministic hard interventions \(z_k=\operatorname{do}(X_{W_k}=w_k)\), including \(W_k=\varnothing\).  If \(M=\varnothing\), first run the published conditional \(\mathsf{CTFID}(G,\mathcal Z,Q)\); if \(M\ne\varnothing\), first run \(\mathsf{MID}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)\).  A successful front end is used only as a sound certificate that the query is constant on compatible positive-denominator menu fibers.  Its expression is not returned unchanged and is not asserted to belong literally to \(\mathcal R(p)\).  Whether the applicable front end succeeds or fails, the oracle's returned functional is compiled by the guarded construction below.

Enumerate at most
\[
 A_{G,M}=\prod_{v\in V}T_v^{\prod_{u\in U_G:\,v\in\operatorname{ch}(u)}b_u}
\]
canonical signed-isotone structural-table profiles.  For each profile \(a\), use product-simplex mass coordinates \(\lambda\).  Under the hard intervention \(z_k\), topological evaluation gives the integer-coefficient polynomial menu cells \(\phi_{a,k,x}(\lambda)\) and the polynomial counterfactual numerator and denominator \(h_a(\lambda)\) and \(d_a(\lambda)\).  Exact real quantifier elimination decides the finite disjunction over profile pairs imposing both product-simplex systems, \(d_{a_0}>0\), \(d_{a_1}>0\), equality of every \(\phi_{a_i,k,x}\), and
\[
 h_{a_0}d_{a_1}\ne h_{a_1}d_{a_0}.
\]
If the disjunction is satisfiable, exact algebraic sample-point extraction records the profiles, masses, sign conditions, common menu vector, and unequal cross-products in \(\tau_{\mathsf F}\), and the oracle returns \((\mathsf{FAIL},\tau_{\mathsf F})\).  If it is unsatisfiable, form
\[
 \Gamma_Q=\{(p,t):\exists a,\lambda,\ \Lambda_a(\lambda),\ p=\phi_a(\lambda),\ d_a(\lambda)>0,\ t d_a(\lambda)=h_a(\lambda)\}.
\]
Use effective sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition and Thom encodings to compile its singleton fibers into a finite expression \(F\in\mathcal R(p)\), and set \(F(p)=0\) off the projection of \(\Gamma_Q\).  Thus a front-end success can skip the nonidentification search after its soundness implication has been checked, but it cannot skip this guarded compilation.  The oracle examines at most \(A_{G,M}\) profiles and \(A_{G,M}^2\) ordered profile pairs; a pair has at most \(2N_{G,M}=2\sum_{u\in U_G}(b_u-1)\) free mass coordinates, and each model sum has at most \(R_{G,M}\) joint latent monomials.  This definition is the global semantic decision and checking substrate; it does not define the unresolved district-local order-AMWN rewrite system or a compiler from a local graphical failure trace.

definitions.name: Cfail
definitions.construction: The failure compiler \(\mathsf C_{\mathsf F}\) is the exact decoder for the algebraic certificate \(\tau_{\mathsf F}\) returned by \(\mathsf{MCTFID}\).  It reads the two enumerated signed-isotone structural-table profiles and their exact algebraic product-simplex masses, deletes zero-mass padding states, and returns the resulting finite canonical models \((\mathfrak m_0,\mathfrak m_1)\) together with the recorded common menu vector \(p^{\star}\).  Before returning, it checks every simplex constraint, every structural-table sign constraint, every menu-cell equality, both strict denominator inequalities, and the unequal query cross-product.  Thus \(\mathsf C_{\mathsf F}\) decodes a globally checkable quantifier-elimination sample certificate; it is not a compiler from a district-local graphical failure trace.

definitions.name: lambdaF
definitions.construction: Traverse the finite expression tree \(F\) at \(p\), retain the guards and algebraic operations on the selected branch, and set \(\lambda_F(p)\) equal to the minimum of the absolute branch-guard values, active division denominators, active isolated-root derivatives, and active root-to-isolating-interval endpoint distances; set \(\lambda_F(p)=1\) if this list is empty.

definitions.name: thetaHat
definitions.construction: For a successful output \(F\in\mathcal R(p)\), evaluate the same finite expression tree at the empirical regime cell vectors: \(\widehat\theta_Q=F(\widehat p)\). On the locally selected branch certified by \(\lambda_F(p)>0\), differentiate sums, products, quotients, and isolated roots recursively to obtain \(\nabla_kF(\widehat p)\) whenever \(\widehat p\) remains on that branch.

definitions.name: plug-in Wald interval
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{CI}_{1-\alpha}=\bigl[\widehat\theta_Q-z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat\sigma_F/\sqrt n,\widehat\theta_Q+z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat\sigma_F/\sqrt n\bigr]\), where \(\widehat\sigma_F^2\) substitutes \(\widehat p_k\), \(n_k/n\), and \(\nabla_kF(\widehat p)\) into \(\sigma_F^2(p)\).

definitions.name: Mpub
definitions.construction:
Define the published common-input binary CGMA class by
\[
 \mathfrak M_{\mathrm{PB}}^{\mathrm{bin}}(G,M)
 =\left\{\mathfrak s=(V,U,F,P_U):
 \begin{array}{l}
 \mathfrak s\text{ is a recursive general SCM whose directed and latent-dependence relations are compatible with }G,\\
 X_v\in\{0,1\}\text{ for every }v\in V,\text{ and }P_U\text{ has full support on its declared exogenous support},\\
 \text{for every }((w,v),+1)\in M,\ f_v(1,x_{-w},u)\ge f_v(0,x_{-w},u),\\
 \text{and for every }((w,v),-1)\in M,\ f_v(1,x_{-w},u)\le f_v(0,x_{-w},u),\\
 \text{for every fixed assignment }x_{-w}\text{ of the other observed parents and every exogenous assignment }u
 \end{array}
 \right\}.
\]
No finite exogenous-support, mutual-independence, private/edge-specific latent expansion, or semi-Markovian restriction is imposed by this definition.  The class concerns only the model; the common deterministic intervention menu and counterfactual query remain separate inputs.

definitions.name: MIDplus
definitions.construction:
For a finite binary unnested conditional query whose numerator is the single literal \(L\), call a literal \(W_{t,s}=b\) parent-fixed when its intervention explicitly assigns every observed parent of \(W\), with \(t\) the sign-normalized assignment of the parents restricted by \(M\), \(s\) the assignment of the remaining parents, and \(b\in\{0,1\}\).  Initialize the signed order closure with the parent-fixed response literals occurring in \(B_Q\); non-parent-fixed conditioning literals remain part of \(B_Q\) but generate no order insertions.  For fixed \(W\) and \(s\), repeatedly apply
\[
 W_{t,s}=1,\ t\le t'
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad W_{t',s}=1,
 \qquad
 W_{t,s}=0,\ t'\le t
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad W_{t',s}=0.
\tag{1}
\]
The fixed point is denoted \(\operatorname{cl}_M(B_Q)\).  If \(L\) is parent-fixed, \(\mathsf{MID}^{+}\) returns the constant one when \(L\in\operatorname{cl}_M(B_Q)\) and the constant zero when \(\overline L\in\operatorname{cl}_M(B_Q)\); in every other case it runs \(\mathsf{MID}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)\).  On a positive-denominator input the first two cases cannot conflict.  There are at most
\[
 2\sum_{v\in V}2^{|\operatorname{pa}_G(v)|}
\]
distinct binary parent-fixed full-parent response literals, so fixed-point saturation terminates after at most that many distinct insertions.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\), there exists a counterfactually equivalent finite \(\widetilde{\mathfrak m}\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\) whose local mechanism at \(v\) uses at most \(T_v=D_{m_v}^{2^{r_v}}\) signed-isotone response types and whose exogenous support satisfies \(|\Omega_u|\le b_u\) for every \(u\in U_G\). Hence every finite menu law and every finite counterfactual law are preserved using at most \(R_{G,M}\) joint latent configurations. If \(m_v>0\), then \(T_v<2^{2^{|\operatorname{pa}_G(v)|}}\), the unrestricted Boolean response-function count.
statements.justification: This theorem converts the shape restriction into an exact finite carrier and exposes the Dedekind-number reduction that all later certification uses.
statements.gap: ZhangTianBareinboim2022 proves finite canonical equivalence using all local response functions; it does not preserve and count a signed-isotone subfamily.
statements.consumer: DuarteEtAl2024 can delete every order-violating response type before constructing a bound program, and MaitiPleckoBareinboim2025 gains an exact finite oracle for implementation tests.

statements.statement: Suppose every regime in \(\mathcal Z\) is the specified deterministic hard intervention \(z_k=\operatorname{do}(X_{W_k}=w_k)\), with \(W_k\subseteq V\) and \(w_k\in\{0,1\}^{W_k}\); \(W_k=\varnothing\) denotes observation. After finite enumeration of the signed-isotone structural tables, the global sentence \(\operatorname{GID}_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(Q)=1\) is decidable by exact real quantifier elimination. Each enumerated pair of canonical models uses at most \(2\sum_{u\in U_G}(b_u-1)\) free exogenous-mass variables and at most \(2R_{G,M}\) joint latent configurations in total. When the sentence is false, the same finite system returns \(\mathfrak m_0,\mathfrak m_1\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\) and their common law \(p^{\star}=P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_0)=P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_1)\), with positive query denominators and \(\theta_Q(\mathfrak m_0)\ne\theta_Q(\mathfrak m_1)\).
statements.justification: This is the exact semantic regression oracle for the specified deterministic hard-intervention menu, with explicit mass dimension and witness size.
statements.gap: Canonical finite-SCM and polynomial-program results provide the main substrate; the signed response-type filtering and exact two-model extraction specialize it to this finite binary conditional-query setting but are not the paper's graphical-completeness kernel.
statements.consumer: Maiti's implementation can use the decision system to check proposed local rules and generate exact failing instances.

statements.statement: For every finite unnested event \(A_Q\cap B_Q\), \(\mathsf N_{G,M}(Q)\) is a unique finite signed sum of order-consistent cells. Each summand factors into one response-type cell per district in \(\mathcal D(G)\), every deleted cell has probability zero in every \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\), and summing the normal form equals \(P_{\mathfrak m}(A_Q\cap B_Q)\) for every such model. The same claim holds for \(B_Q\).
statements.justification: A canonical order normal form is the bridge between local monotonicity identities and district-level identification requests.
statements.gap: CorreaBareinboim2025 makes counterfactual independences explicit in an AMWN, and MaitiPleckoBareinboim2025 reduces selected ordered pairs, but neither supplies a unique signed order-cell normal form with district factorization.
statements.consumer: The AMWN and ctf-calculus toolchain can use this normal form as a deterministic intermediate representation for symbolic identification and audit trails.

statements.statement: Construct \(\mathsf{MCTFID}\) and \(\mathsf C_{\mathsf F}\) from Definitions \(\mathrm{def:mctfid\text{-}handle}\) and \(\mathrm{def:fail\text{-}compiler\text{-}handle}\) such that, for every \((G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)\): \(\mathsf{MCTFID}\) terminates after visiting at most \((|\mathcal D(G)|+K+1)2^{R_{G,M}}\) memoized order cells; it returns one globally defined \(F\in\mathcal R(p)\) if and only if \(\operatorname{GID}_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(Q)=1\), and then \(F(P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m))=\theta_Q(\mathfrak m)\) for every \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,M)\) with \(P_{\mathfrak m}(B_Q)>0\). Otherwise it returns \((\mathsf{FAIL},\tau_{\mathsf F})\), and \(\mathsf C_{\mathsf F}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q,\tau_{\mathsf F})=(\mathfrak m_0,\mathfrak m_1,p^{\star})\) consists of two finite district-factorized signed-isotone SCMs with \(|\Omega_u|\le b_u\), common law \(P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_0)=p^{\star}=P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m_1)\), positive query denominators, and distinct values of \(\theta_Q\). Require also extensional equality with \(\mathsf{CTFID}\) when \(M=\varnothing\), reproduction of every successful \(\mathsf{MID}\) output, and either an explicit instance where the inclusion of \(\mathsf{MID}\) successes is strict or a proof that it is equality.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: a complete symbolic calculus is valuable only if success has an evaluable functional and failure has a legal order-respecting countermodel.
statements.gap: MaitiPleckoBareinboim2025 explicitly leaves a sufficient-and-necessary monotonicity algorithm open; CorreaLeeBareinboim2021 and RaghavanBareinboim2026 prove unrestricted completeness with converse gadgets that do not preserve signed isotonicity.
statements.consumer: Maiti's M-ID implementation receives a complete certified back end, while the PleckoBareinboim2024 Fairness Map receives identifying formulas or explicit impossibility certificates for its finite binary contrasts.

statements.statement: When \(M=\varnothing\), for every \(v\in V\) one has \(m_v=0\), \(r_v=|\operatorname{pa}_G(v)|\), \(D_0=2\), and therefore \(T_v=D_0^{2^{r_v}}=2^{2^{|\operatorname{pa}_G(v)|}}\), exactly the unrestricted Boolean response-function count. All order annotations are then vacuous, and \(\mathsf N_{G,\varnothing}(Q)\) is the ordinary AMWN event normalization. On the common finite-binary recursive semi-Markovian domain, \(\mathsf{MCTFID}(G,\varnothing,\mathcal Z,Q)\) and \(\mathsf{CTFID}(G,\mathcal Z,Q)\) have the same success set. More precisely, whenever \(\mathsf{CTFID}(G,\mathcal Z,Q)\) succeeds and the completed procedure returns \(\mathsf{MCTFID}(G,\varnothing,\mathcal Z,Q)=F\), the successful \(\mathsf{CTFID}\) output and \(F\) both evaluate at \(P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m)\) to \(\theta_Q(\mathfrak m)\) for every \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M(G,\varnothing)\) with \(P_{\mathfrak m}(B_Q)>0\). No equality of the two expression trees, or of their extensions away from compatible positive-denominator menu laws, is asserted.
statements.justification: The theorem gives a noncircular regression test: the response atoms collapse exactly to the unrestricted atoms, while the completed global oracle and conditional CTFID have the same success set and agree extensionally on compatible positive-denominator laws.
statements.gap: CorreaLeeBareinboim2021 supplies unrestricted conditional completeness; the new step is the exact empty-sign collapse of the signed type system and the canonical countermodel transfer into the finite oracle.
statements.consumer: Implementers can use ordinary CTFID outputs as extensional regression tests for every empty-sign execution.

statements.statement: If \(\mathsf{MCTFID}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)=F\in\mathcal R(p)\), then under \(\mathrm{ass:menu\text{-}compatibility}\), \(\mathrm{ass:positive\text{-}query\text{-}denominator}\), \(\mathrm{ass:independent\text{-}regime\text{-}sampling}\), \(\mathrm{ass:stable\text{-}regime\text{-}shares}\), \(\mathrm{ass:analytic\text{-}branch\text{-}margin}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:nondegenerate\text{-}variance}\), the empirical vector remains on the branch selected at \(p\) with probability tending to one and \(\sqrt n\{F(\widehat p)-F(p)\}\rightsquigarrow N(0,\sigma_F^2(p))\). For every generating \(\mathfrak m\in\mathcal F_{G,M,\mathcal Z}(p)\), the branch-local recursively differentiated variance estimator is consistent and \(P_{\mathfrak m}\{\theta_Q(\mathfrak m)\in\mathsf{CI}_{1-\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha\).
statements.justification: A complete identification calculus needs a generic route from finite menu cells to uncertainty quantification under the same denominator conditions used by the query.
statements.gap: BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022 compiles ordinary hidden-variable effect formulas into estimators, while MaitiPleckoBareinboim2025 reports bootstrap intervals without a limit theorem for arbitrary successful signed counterfactual formulas.
statements.consumer: Analysts using the Causal Fairness Analysis toolkit can attach reproducible standard errors and Wald intervals to any fixed successful finite-cell output.

sampling_model.design: \(K\) independent regime-specific multinomial samples from the known observational or interventional menu \(\mathcal Z\).
sampling_model.units: Regime \(k\) contains \(n_k\) independent units with cell law \(p_k\), and \(n_k/n\to\rho_k\in(0,1)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Each regime fixes its declared intervention \(z_k\); the empty intervention is observational sampling.
sampling_model.overlap: The query denominator is bounded below by \(\kappa>0\) on the sampling-law fiber, and the local analytic margin \(\lambda_F(p)\) bounds branch guards, active denominators, root derivatives, and isolating-interval separation away from zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nonparametric nuisance is introduced; every input is a finite empirical cell vector, and differentiation is recursive on the locally fixed analytic branch of the returned expression tree.

estimand_functional: \(\theta_Q(\mathfrak m)=F(P_{\mathcal Z}(\mathfrak m))\) when \(\mathsf{MCTFID}(G,M,\mathcal Z,Q)=F\), with \(\widehat\theta_Q=F(\widehat p)\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: M-ID is sound on its published ordered-variable and general-SCM CGMA domain and leaves a sufficient-and-necessary general algorithm open.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: On common binary inputs, the antichain/join theorem proves a pointwise identified family missed by Algorithms 1--2 and a sound order-closure precheck; decoded oracle failures transfer upward, but oracle success remains restricted to the narrower finite-binary semi-Markovian class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Conditional CTFID is sound and complete without signed monotonicity restrictions for observational and experimental input laws.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The empty-sign response-type collapse and extensional success-set comparison on the common deterministic hard-intervention binary domain.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Finite discrete counterfactual laws admit counterfactually equivalent canonical finite SCM representations using unrestricted response functions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The signed canonical reduction filters local Boolean tables to signed-isotone up-sets and proves the strict Dedekind-count reduction when a signed parent is present.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: AMWNs expose counterfactual independences and support ctf-calculus transformations without the present signed-order completeness claim.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The order-normal factorization theorem and the unresolved graphical-compression obligation.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper studies completeness and bounding with realizable Layer-3 counterfactual input data.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Adjacent completeness context only; it is not characterized as a Layer-1 or Layer-2 menu-law parity-gadget converse for this problem.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Complete identification methods are given for unrestricted levels of the causal hierarchy.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Background for unrestricted necessity; the present signed shape constraints alter the legal response types and do not inherit that graphical converse automatically.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: General identifiability with arbitrary surrogate experiments is characterized in the unrestricted causal model.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Background for menu and district recursion; the current oracle is restricted to specified deterministic hard interventions and signed binary response tables.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Discrete causal queries can be represented by finite polynomial programs.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The finite response-profile decision theorem is an exact signed conditional-query specialization and is treated as checking substrate rather than the graphical novelty claim.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Monotonicity bounds and identification are studied for joint potential-outcome and observed-variable probabilities in a single-treatment ordinal setting.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: A distinct arbitrary-diagram, hard-intervention-menu, signed local-mechanism target; no dominance over the single-treatment bounds is claimed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Identified hidden-variable graphical functionals can be connected to semiparametric estimation.

tldr: For finite binary semi-Markovian diagrams, local signed monotonicity deletes most Boolean response functions but invalidates the parity countermodels used in unrestricted completeness proofs. The project first proves a signed canonical finite-SCM reduction with an explicit Dedekind-number support bound and a global semialgebraic identification oracle. Its open kernel is to compress that oracle into a terminating district-compositional \(\mathsf{MCTFID}\) calculus built from an order-annotated AMWN and canonical order-normal cells, with one menu-law functional exactly for globally identified queries and a failed trace compiled into two legal signed-isotone SCMs together with their common observable law. The calculus must reduce to ordinary CTFID when \(M=\varnothing\), reproduce every M-ID success, expose whether that inclusion is strict, and feed a locally branch-stable finite-cell central limit theorem and Wald interval.

project_justification.gap: MaitiPleckoBareinboim2025 proves sound monotonicity reductions but explicitly leaves a sufficient-and-necessary general algorithm open. Unrestricted completeness proofs in CorreaLeeBareinboim2021 and RaghavanBareinboim2026 use countermodels whose parity mechanisms violate signed local monotonicity, while canonical finite-SCM programs do not yield a district-compositional identifying calculus.
project_justification.niche: The finite binary setting admits exact order geometry: after sign normalization, each local response table is an up-set of a Boolean lattice and has a Dedekind-number count. This creates a finite oracle and a concrete target for replacing parity with composable threshold atoms without narrowing the published signed-monotone model class.
project_justification.fill: The project builds a canonical order-normal AMWN representation, proves its district factorization, derives a terminating complete symbolic procedure with explicit state and response-type bounds, and requires every failure to carry two finite order-respecting SCMs and their common menu law. A multisample delta method on a certified locally fixed analytic branch then turns every fixed successful expression into an empirical-cell estimator and confidence interval.

related_work: MaitiPleckoBareinboim2025 supplies the writing arc and the local monotonicity reduction and difference rules, but its conclusion identifies full necessity and sufficiency as the missing endpoint. CorreaLeeBareinboim2021 supplies counterfactual unnesting, ancestral reduction, district factorization, and complete CTFID for arbitrary observational and interventional menus. CorreaBareinboim2025 supplies the AMWN construction and ctf-calculus transformations that the order annotations refine. RaghavanBareinboim2026 supplies the closest failure-to-countermodel compiler, but its mod-two parent sums and flipped parity bit are not isotone. ZhangTianBareinboim2022 supplies the canonical finite-SCM equivalence proof; restricting its canonical partitions to signed-isotone response functions yields the proposed Dedekind count. LeeCorreaBareinboim2020 and ShpitserPearl2008 explain how hedgelets, thickets, and district recursion certify unrestricted necessity. DuarteEtAl2024 supplies a general polynomial-program oracle against which the graphical calculus can be regression-tested. BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022 supplies the identification-to-estimation compiler pattern, while PleckoBareinboim2024 supplies the direct, indirect, spurious, and variable-specific counterfactual consumer family. HashimotoKawakamiTian2026 studies monotonicity bounds for a single-treatment ordinal potential-outcome setting and does not occupy the arbitrary-diagram, arbitrary-menu signed calculus target.
technical_internal_limitation: A finite canonical parameterization makes global identification decidable by real algebraic methods, so mere decidability is not the novelty claim. The load-bearing claim is district-compositional compression with a checkable signed countermodel trace. Restricting successful outputs to rational expressions could be false because finite polynomial model classes can identify algebraic but non-rational functions; the grammar therefore includes uniquely isolated real roots and requires ordinary CTFID outputs as the rational special case. Inference is asserted only where every branch guard and active algebraic operation is separated from its singular boundary by \(\lambda_F(p)\ge\kappa\).
honest_scope: The signed canonical reduction, global finite decision theorem, order-normal factorization, explicit empty-sign reduction, and locally branch-stable plug-in limit are theorem targets with direct finite constructions. The genuinely open content is the composable threshold countermodel compiler and the equivalence between its terminal obstructions and every globally nonidentified graph-menu-query instance. The sanity reduction recomputes \(D_0=2\) and \(T_v=2^{2^{|\operatorname{pa}_G(v)|}}\) when \(M=\varnothing\), after which the procedure must agree extensionally with ordinary CTFID; every M-ID success must also be reproduced. The scope excludes nested syntax before unnesting, continuous endogenous variables, zero conditioning denominators, inference at branch boundaries, and data-dependent selection among empirically tied formulas.
